findings_addressed.oracle: Windows VirtualQueryEx API specification: page sizes are always multiples of 0x1000, states are drawn from {MEM_COMMIT=0x1000, MEM_RESERVE=0x2000, MEM_FREE=0x10000}, protections are drawn from documented PAGE_* constants. All-zero stub tuples now fail size-alignment and state/protection membership checks.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/bridges/hex_editor.py HexEditorProcessMemoryMixin.list_process_regions, change `return [{'base_address': r[0], 'size': r[1], 'protection': r[2], 'state': r[3]} for r in regions]` to `return [{'base_address': 0, 'size': 0, 'protection': 0, 'state': 0} for _ in regions]` — the new assertions `r['size'] > 0`, `r['size'] % 0x1000 == 0`, `r['state'] in known_states`, and `r['protection'] in known_protections` all fail.

findings_addressed.oracle: Windows memory model: a running CPython interpreter will always have far more than 10 MEM_COMMIT regions (heap, stack, code, DLLs, private data). A single hardcoded stub region now fails the `len(committed) > 10` threshold.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/bridges/hex_editor.py HexEditorProcessMemoryMixin.list_process_regions, replace the real VirtualQueryEx enumeration with `return [{'base_address': 0x1000, 'size': 0x1000, 'protection': 0x04, 'state': 0x1000}]` — `len(committed) > 10` fails because only 1 committed region is returned.
